value: Causal language model with 2.4T total and 95B activated parameters, 92 layers, hidden dimension 8192, hidden layout 23 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → MoE) → 1 × (Gated Attention → MoE)); Mixture of Experts with 512 experts (10 routed + 1 shared activated); built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5. The card gives no explicit rationale for the design choices.

value: The card has no dedicated limitations or risks section. It does state some technical constraints. The model is text-only, multimodal inputs are not supported, and thinking cannot be disabled. Endless repetition can occur. Raising presence_penalty to reduce it may occasionally cause language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance.
quote: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is a text-only model that requires thinking mode for all interactions. Multimodal inputs are not supported, and thinking cannot be disabled. [...] For supported frameworks, you can adjust the `presence_penalty` parameter between 0 and 2 to reduce endless repetition. However, using a higher value may occasionally result in language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance.
quotes: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is a text-only model that requires thinking mode for all interactions. Multimodal inputs are not supported, and thinking cannot be disabled.

For supported frameworks, you can adjust the `presence_penalty` parameter between 0 and 2 to reduce endless repetition. However, using a higher value may occasionally result in language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance.

value: Benchmark footnotes give per-benchmark methodology. Terminal Bench 2.1 was evaluated with Claude Code (avg@10), a 5-hour timeout and max_tokens=131,072. SWE-bench Pro was evaluated with the Claude Code harness, temp=1.0, top_p=0.95 and a 256K context window. QwenSWEBench was evaluated with the Claude Code harness, avg@3, an 8-hour timeout, max_tokens=32,768, temperature=1.0 and a 256K-token context window. SkillsBench was evaluated on OpenCode for the Qwen-series (public v1.1, 87 tasks, average over three runs per task). WideSearch used the Qwen-Agent harness for Qwen's own model, reporting average item-F1 over four runs.
